title: Standard Library Tour
description: An overview of frequently used standard library modules and what each one is for.
objectives: Know the purpose of the most commonly used standard library modules
Recognize when to reach for the standard library instead of writing something from scratch

content.heading: Core Utility Modules
content.body: math provides mathematical functions and constants beyond the built-in operators: sqrt(), floor(), ceil(), pi, and more. random generates pseudo-random numbers and makes random choices/shuffles — random.randint(a, b), random.choice(seq), random.shuffle(list). datetime represents dates, times, and durations, and supports formatting/parsing between text and datetime objects. os provides operating-system interaction: environment variables, process info, and (older-style) path manipulation, while pathlib offers a more modern, object-oriented way to work with filesystem paths (Path("data") / "file.txt" instead of manual string joining). sys exposes interpreter-level state and controls: command-line arguments (sys.argv), the module search path (sys.path), and standard streams.

content.heading: Data-Handling Modules
content.body: json serializes Python objects to/from the JSON text format — dumps()/loads() for strings, dump()/load() for files (covered in depth in the JSON and CSV lesson). csv reads and writes comma-separated value files without you needing to hand-roll splitting/quoting logic. collections extends the built-in container types with specialized variants: Counter (counting hashable items), defaultdict (a dict with automatic default values for missing keys), namedtuple (lightweight, immutable records with named fields), and deque (a double-ended queue with fast appends/pops on either end). itertools provides efficient, composable building blocks for iteration: chain(), product(), combinations(), permutations(), and more, all working lazily. functools offers tools for working with functions themselves, including reduce() (seen earlier) and lru_cache (automatic memoization).

content.code:
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
import itertools

print(Counter("mississippi"))          # Counter({'i': 4, 's': 4, 'p': 2, 'm': 1})

groups = defaultdict(list)
groups["fruit"].append("apple")         # no KeyError — defaultdict creates [] automatically
print(dict(groups))

print(list(itertools.product([0, 1], repeat=2)))   # [(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)]
content.explanation: Counter tallies character frequencies in one call. defaultdict(list) avoids needing to check 'does this key exist yet' before appending. itertools.product generates the Cartesian product lazily.

keyPoints: math/random cover numeric and randomness needs; datetime handles dates/times
pathlib is the modern, object-oriented way to work with filesystem paths
collections adds Counter, defaultdict, namedtuple, and deque beyond the built-in containers
itertools and functools provide efficient, composable, lazy tools for iteration and function manipulation
commonMistakes: Hand-rolling functionality (like CSV parsing or counting) that the standard library already provides robustly
Reaching for os.path string joining instead of the more readable, cross-platform pathlib
Not knowing collections.Counter/defaultdict exist and writing more verbose manual equivalents
